```{r number-setup}
source(file.path(template_dir, "_numeric-common.R"), local = TRUE)
by_year <- numeric_by_year(st)
check_table(value_checks(xp, st, ev$values[xpath %in% xp$xpath], ev$shapes[xpath %in% xp$xpath], rtype, skip_year = partial_year(ev$filings)))
sc <- st[!is.na(q99), .(p99 = stats::median(q99), n = sum(n_filings)), by = series][n >= 30]
sc[, scale := fifelse(p99 <= 1, "fraction (0-1)", fifelse(p99 <= 100, "percent or small count", "large count or amount"))]
```

```{r number-plot, fig.height = 3.8}
if (nrow(by_year)) {
  print(numeric_plot(copy(by_year), log_scale = FALSE, title = "Typical value by tax year", ylab = NULL))
  html_table(by_year[order(series, return_type, tax_year), .(Series = series, Return = return_type, `Tax year` = tax_year,
                                                             Filings = n, P25 = q25, Median = q50, P75 = q75)],
             caption = "Table view: quartiles by tax year", collapse = TRUE)
}
```

```{r number-summary}
html_table(numeric_summary(st), caption = "Summary by xpath and return type (all years)", digits = 2)
html_table(sc[, .(Series = series, `P99 (typical year)` = p99, `Implied scale` = scale)], caption = "Scale of each xpath")
checklist <- c(
  "Counts are whole numbers and plausible (e.g. employees, volunteers, voting members).",
  "Ratios and percentages use one scale (0-1 or 0-100) across all xpaths and years.",
  "Units match the form line (hours per week, number of states, percent of support)."
)
```
